brief: Nine systems read season() and every one of them is west of the bridge or in the sky. The plaza is identical in February and August — the exact position the market was in before #29. The fountain is the plaza’s landmark and has no seasonal reader at all. Give it the year: what the water does, what the basin looks like, and who is willing to stand near it should not be the same in midwinter as in midsummer. NOTE: issued at #35 and consumed by a harness fault before any worker ran — no prior attempt exists. Since #32 the bandstand DOES read the year (bandChance off warmth), so the plaza is now the only east-of-bridge place that does not.
successLooksLike: A pinned midwinter and a pinned midsummer plaza differ visibly in the wide shot, and the difference is continuous — a probe over a folded year shows no step in the fountain terms at any phase, and every term reduces exactly to today’s constant at SEASON_START.
avoid: riverRun() already exists for the water and reads the same year — read it or a sibling of it; do not re-derive a second water-season term (one predicate, one definition). Do not let a global scalar approach zero without per-cell variance or it reads as a switch. And check what the fountain was tuned against before making its constants variable: crumbSpot’s keep-rect reads waterBox off the grid, and #24 put 22 birds in the basin the last time two places evaluated the same geometry.
